rules.title: New Jersey FAIR Act (Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent Act)
rules.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not use algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices. Software providers and other "coordinators" may not use such software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords. The attorney general must set up a complaint portal, and existing remedies under the New Jersey Antitrust Act are preserved.
rules.key_value: Takes effect July 1, 2027; AG complaint portal; New Jersey Antitrust Act remedies preserved

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental property owners and to software providers/coordinators using nonpublic competitively sensitive data from multiple residential rental owners.
coverage.other_conditions: Does not prohibit spreadsheets requiring human analysis, publicly available rent estimation tools, traditional real estate listing databases, or government-administered affordable housing programs.

rules.exemptions: Spreadsheets requiring human analysis, publicly available rent estimation tools, traditional real estate listing databases, and government-administered affordable housing programs are not prohibited.
citation_aliases: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent Act
rules.quoted_span: The FAIR Act takes effect on July 1, 2027, providing affected property owners, managers, and software providers time to review and, if necessary, modify their pricing practices before the law becomes effective.
rules.review_note: Secondary source (law-firm alert); codified section not given. Whether the Act preempts local ordinances (Jersey City, Hoboken) is not addressed in this document.

result.doc_summary: Day Pitney law-firm alert reporting that NJ Governor Sherrill signed the FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c. 43) on July 20, banning use of algorithmic revenue management software that uses competitors' nonpublic leasing data to set rents, and barring coordinators from facilitating coordinated pricing. It sets up an AG complaint portal, preserves Antitrust Act remedies, and takes effect July 1, 2027.
